mainTopic: Betrothing with a loan (מקדש במלוה): defending רב, the status of unspent loan money, and transferring a שטר חוב for קידושין
overview: Just before this amud, the גמרא challenged רב, who holds that קידושין with a loan does not work, from a ברייתא about betrothing with a deposit or a loan. רבא answers that the ברייתא's wording is faulty. He proves this by asking what kind of deposit it means, and he corrects it to say that a loan never works for קידושין. Next the גמרא asks what רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view, 'a loan is like a deposit,' is really about. רבה rejects the idea that the argument covers responsibility for accidents, since a borrower is surely liable for them. He concludes that the תנאים argue only about whether a lender can take back unspent loan money. The גמרא then shows that רב הונא's rule about a borrowed ax fits everyone, because a borrowed object comes back as itself. Finally, the גמרא asks whether רב's rule is a dispute between רבי מאיר and חכמים about קידושין with a שטר חוב. It rejects this by explaining that their argument is about transferring someone else's debt. It gives explanations based on רבי, then רב פפא, and begins a third based on שמואל, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Everyone in the ברייתא seems to agree a loan works
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes with the view that a loan is like a deposit. The challenger argues that the opinions only disagree about whether a פרוטה must remain, so all agree that קידושין with a loan works. This contradicts רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: '…is like a deposit.' The two Sages disagree only about this: one Sage holds that a loan works even if not a פרוטה's worth of it remains. The other Sage holds that if a פרוטה's worth remains it works, and if not, it does not. But everyone agrees that if a man betroths with a loan, she is betrothed!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא quote ends, and the challenger draws a conclusion from it. Both opinions in the ברייתא accept that a loan can work for קידושין, which goes against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two views argue only about a detail: must a פרוטה's worth of the loan still exist? Arguing about that detail assumes that a loan can work in principle. That shared assumption contradicts רב, who says מקדש במלוה אינה מקודשת.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit: an item left with someone to look after
A loan, money given to be spent and later paid back
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest value that counts for קידושין
Remained, is still left over
Everyone, all opinions
She is betrothed

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge does not come from what either side says outright. It comes from what both sides take for granted while arguing about the פרוטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted before this passage and draws the challenge against רב from it
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that קידושין with a loan does not work
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions in the ברייתא argue only about whether a פרוטה must remain. That assumes a loan works in principle, which contradicts רב.

steps.title: רבא says the ברייתא's wording is broken
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof. He says the ברייתא as worded does not make sense, so it cannot be used as evidence.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Do you really think this ברייתא is in proper order? It is garbled!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the challenge. He claims the ברייתא's text is faulty, and he is about to prove it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is not arguing with the challenger's logic. He is attacking the source itself: if the wording is wrong, nothing can be proven from it. The next step shows why the wording cannot stand.

keyTerms.meaning: In proper order, well-worded
Garbled, with faulty wording

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
And do you think this is properly worded?
It is garbled.

steps.triggerLanguage: ותסברא הא מתרצתא הא משבשתא היא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the ברייתא as worded, not the logic of the inference
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The text of the ברייתא is faulty and cannot serve as proof

steps.title: Proving the ברייתא's wording cannot be right
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what kind of deposit the ברייתא means. If she accepted responsibility for it, the deposit is really a loan. If she did not, the ברייתא should have made that distinction inside the deposit case itself instead of adding a separate loan clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of this deposit? If she accepted responsibility for it, it is the same as a loan. If she did not accept responsibility, then instead of teaching in the last part, 'with a loan, even if a פרוטה's worth does not remain, she is betrothed,' the ברייתא should have made the distinction within the deposit case itself: 'When is this said? When she did not accept responsibility. But if she did accept responsibility, even if a פרוטה's worth does not remain, she is betrothed!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his claim that the ברייתא is garbled. He shows that both ways of understanding the deposit leave the current wording making no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: a deposit she is responsible for is basically a loan, so the deposit and loan clauses could not have different rules. Option two: if the deposit is one with no responsibility, the natural way to teach the contrast would be within the deposit case, 'with responsibility it works.' Because the ברייתא did neither, its last clause about a loan must be worded wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Financial responsibility to pay if the item is lost or stolen
What is the case? What are the details?
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
Let it make the distinction and teach it within the same case
When is this said? A phrase that limits a ruling

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'she accepted responsibility' means the woman holding the man's deposit agreed to pay him if it got lost. That makes it work like a loan she owes him.

If she accepted responsibility for it,

If she did not accept responsibility for it,

When she did not accept responsibility upon herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's claim in step 2 that the ברייתא is garbled
steps.kashyaTarget: The current wording of the ברייתא's last clause about a loan
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both readings of the deposit case leave the separate loan clause either redundant or oddly placed, so the wording must be wrong.

steps.title: The corrected wording: a loan does not work
steps.stepSummary: רבא corrects the ברייתא's last clause. With a loan she is not betrothed, even if a פרוטה's worth of it remains. This fits רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, correct it this way: 'And with a loan, even though a פרוטה's worth of it remains, she is not betrothed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the right wording of the ברייתא. In his version, קידושין with a loan does not work at all, so the challenge to רב falls away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new wording sets up a clear contrast: a deposit works if a פרוטה's worth remains, but a loan never works, even when something remains. A loan was already given to her to spend, so it is no longer his money to give. The ברייתא now supports רב instead of contradicting him.

keyTerms.meaning: Correct the wording this way
She is not betrothed

steps.whatToRemember: רבא answers the challenge to רב by fixing the ברייתא's wording. A loan does not work for קידושין even if a פרוטה's worth remains, while a deposit works if a פרוטה's worth remains.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps רב's rule that מקדש במלוה אינה מקודשת. It also shows the clear difference between a deposit, which still belongs to the man, and a loan, which belongs to the borrower to spend.

phrases.english: Rather, correct it this way:
'And with a loan, even though
a פרוטה's worth of it remains,
she is not betrothed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the corrected wording that step 3 showed was needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says a loan works for קידושין even if no פרוטה remains, which contradicts רב
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא should say a loan does not work even if a פרוטה remains, which agrees with רב

steps.title: What is the disagreement about a loan really about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view that a loan is like a deposit. It then asks what principle the two sides of the ברייתא are actually arguing over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי מאיר: a loan is like a deposit. About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the last line of the ברייתא and asks what the real point of disagreement is. This sets up רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the steps before this one, the גמרא looked at this ברייתא as it relates to קידושין. Now it wants the underlying legal idea behind the disagreement. The question is how each side views the status of loaned money that has not yet been spent.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan of money, which the borrower is expected to spend and repay with other money
A deposit: something left with a person for safekeeping, which still belongs to the owner
About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says
in the name of Rabbi Meir:
A loan is like a deposit.
About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the קידושין proof (steps 1-4) to the underlying principle of the ברייתא's disagreement
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What legal principle separates the תנא קמא from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר regarding a loan

steps.title: The scholars in רב's study hall: they disagree about taking the loan back and about accidents
steps.stepSummary: רבה reports what the scholars in בית רב said. The disagreement is over whether an unspent loan is still in the lender's possession. That would decide two things: whether the lender can take it back, and who carries the risk of אונסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: I found the scholars in רב's study hall sitting and saying that they disagree about whether a loan is in the owner's possession for taking it back, and the same goes for accidents. One master holds that a loan is in the borrower's possession, and the same for accidents. The other master holds that a loan is in the owner's possession, and the same for accidents.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה tells us an answer he heard from other scholars. In their view, the two תנאים disagree about who "holds" an unspent loan: the borrower or the lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the loan belongs to the borrower. So the lender cannot take it back, and if it is lost the borrower carries the loss. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says it still belongs to the lender, which is why he compares it to a פקדון. On this reading, both the right to take it back and the risk of loss go with that one question.

keyTerms.meaning: In the possession (domain) of the owner, here the lender
In the possession of the borrower
Taking back: whether the lender can demand the loan back before it is spent
Accidents beyond one's control, such as theft or loss. The question is who carries the loss.
The study hall of רב

phrases.english: Rabba said:
I found the scholars in the study hall of Rav
who were sitting and saying:
About whether a loan is in the owner's possession with regard to taking it back
phrases.notes: "The owner" here means the lender. The question is whether he can still demand the money before it is spent.

phrases.english: and the same goes for accidents, they disagree.
For one master holds:
A loan stands in the borrower's possession,
and the same is true for accidents.
And the other master holds:
A loan stands in the owner's possession,
and the same is true for accidents.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכַּחְתִּינְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן בְּבֵי רַב דְּיָתְבִי וְקָאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by reporting the view of the scholars in בית רב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנאים disagree about whether an unspent loan is in the lender's or the borrower's possession, both for taking it back and for responsibility for accidents

steps.title: Everyone agrees the borrower is responsible for accidents
steps.stepSummary: רבה disagrees with the scholars. Responsibility for accidents cannot be part of the מחלוקת. A borrower of an object is already liable for accidents, so a borrower of money must be liable all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I said to them: about accidents, everyone agrees it is in the borrower's possession. Why? A loan is no worse than borrowing an object. If someone who borrows an object, which goes back to the owner exactly as it was, is liable for accidents, then a loan certainly makes him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה rejects half of the scholars' explanation. He proves with a קל וחומר that nobody could say the lender carries the risk of accidents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שואל gives back the very same item, and still the תורה makes him liable for אונסין. A person who borrows money spends it and pays back with other money, so the money is even more truly his. This means the risk of accidents must be his according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees; there is no disagreement
Borrowing an object, which is then returned itself
As it is: the very same item
All the more so

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up שְׁאֵלָה (borrowing an object and giving back that same object) with מִלְוָה (borrowing money that you spend and repay with other money). רבה's argument depends on that difference.

phrases.english: And I said to them:
Regarding accidents, everyone agrees
that it stands in the borrower's possession.
What is the reason? It is no worse than borrowing an object.
Just as with a borrowed object, which is returned exactly as it was,
he is liable for accidents,
phrases.notes: This is the תורה's rule for a borrower in שמות 22:13.

phrases.english: then with a loan, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמֵינָא לְהוּ לָאוֹנָסִים כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the accidents part of the explanation given in step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the claim that the תנאים disagree about responsibility for accidents
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores the קל וחומר from שאלה: a borrower of an object is liable for accidents, so a borrower of money certainly is

steps.title: The real disagreement is only about taking the loan back
steps.stepSummary: רבה concludes that the two תנאים disagree only about whether the lender can take back a loan that has not yet been spent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between them here is whether a loan is in the owner's possession with regard to taking it back.
steps.whatsHappening: Having removed the accidents part, רבה states what the מחלוקת is really about: whether the lender can take back unspent loan money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, the lender cannot take it back. According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, he can, since for this purpose the money is still "his," like a פקדון. That is also why רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds he could use it for קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them; this is the point they disagree about

steps.whatToRemember: On רבה's reading, everyone agrees the borrower carries the risk of accidents. The two תנאים disagree only about whether the lender can take back unspent loan money.

phrases.english: Rather, here
whether a loan is in the owner's possession with regard to taking it back
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכָא מִלְוָה בִּרְשׁוּת בְּעָלִים לַחֲזָרָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבה's corrected version of the disagreement after rejecting the accidents part in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים disagree about both taking the loan back and accidents
steps.terutzMaskana: They disagree only about whether the lender can take back an unspent loan

steps.title: Does רב הונא's rule about a borrowed ax depend on this disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב הונא's rule: if someone borrowed an ax and chopped with it, the lender cannot take it back early, but if he did not chop yet, the lender can. It asks whether רב הונא is just taking one side of the תנאים' disagreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about רב הונא's statement: one who borrows an ax from his friend, if he chopped with it, he acquired it; if he did not chop with it, he did not acquire it. Shall we say he stated his teaching according to one side of a disagreement between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with רבה's explanation. It sets up a discussion of whether רב הונא's rule fits both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says that a borrowed item that has not yet been used can be taken back by the lender. That sounds like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who says unspent loan money can be taken back. If so, רב הונא would only fit one תנא, and the תנא קמא would disagree. The גמרא does not like to say an אמורא's rule follows only one side unless it has to.

keyTerms.meaning: An ax
He chopped (split wood)
He acquired it: here, the lender can no longer take it back before the agreed time
Shall we say it follows one side of a disagreement between תנאים?

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא tries to show that an אמורא's rule fits everyone. So it will need to explain how רב הונא can agree with both תנאים.

phrases.english: But then, that which Rav Huna said:
One who borrows an ax from his friend,
if he chopped with it, he has acquired it.
phrases.notes: "Acquired" here doesn't mean he owns the ax. It means the lender can't take it back before the agreed time.

phrases.english: If he did not chop with it, he has not acquired it.
Shall we say he stated his teaching according to one side of a disagreement between tanna'im?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבה's conclusion in step 8 to question whether רב הונא's rule depends on a מחלוקת between תנאים
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ax rule, which on רבה's explanation would seem to follow only רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תנאים disagree about whether an unused loan can be taken back, then רב הונא's rule that an unused borrowed ax can be taken back would fit only רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and the תנא קמא would disagree with him

steps.title: A borrowed ax is different from a loan of money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב הונא does not depend on the תנאים. They argue only about a loan, which is not returned as is. With a borrowed object, which is returned as is, everyone agrees with רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The תנאים only argue about a loan, because loaned money does not come back as the same coins. With a borrowed object, which comes back as the same item, everyone agrees: if he chopped with it, he has acquired the use of it; if he did not chop, he has not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9. רב הונא is not taking sides, because the תנאים' argument does not cover borrowed objects at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loaned money is meant to be spent, and the borrower pays back with other coins. That is why the תנאים can argue about whether the loan has already left the lender's hands. A borrowed ax comes back as the very same ax, so the borrower only 'takes hold' of it once he actually uses it. On that point everyone agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes back as it is: the very same item is returned
Borrowing an object, which must be returned as is
Everyone agrees
Chopped (with the ax)

steps.whatToRemember: A מלוה (money loan) is spent and repaid with other money. A שאלה (borrowed object) comes back as the same item. The argument of the תנאים is only about מלוה.

phrases.english: No, they only disagree
about a loan,
which does not come back as it is.
phrases.notes: He means the borrower pays back with other coins, not the same ones he got.

phrases.english: But with a borrowed object,
which does come back as it is,
everyone agrees:
if he chopped with it, yes;
if he did not chop with it, he has not acquired it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא בְּמִלְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 by limiting the תנאים' dispute to money loans.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (loan of money vs. borrowed object)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא's ax rule follows only one side of the תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנאים argue only about loaned money. For a borrowed object everyone agrees it is acquired only once it is used.

steps.title: Is the rule about קידושין with a loan a dispute of תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the rule that a man cannot be מקדש with a loan depends on a ברייתא where רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about קידושין with a שטר חוב or a debt owed by others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a dispute of תנאים? A ברייתא teaches: if a man says 'Be מקודשת to me with a שטר חוב,' or he had a debt owed to him by others and gave her the right to collect it, רבי מאיר says she is מקודשת and חכמים say she is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to suggest that the rule 'one cannot be מקדש with a loan' is really only one side of a dispute between תנאים. This step sets up the evidence, and the next step builds the argument from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule of the סוגיא is that קידושין with a loan does not work. If רבי מאיר holds she is מקודשת with a שטר חוב, that rule would match only חכמים. The proof depends on which שטר חוב the ברייתא means, and the next step explains that.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it is a dispute between תנאים?
A written document recording a debt
He gave her the right (to collect the debt)
She is betrothed (the קידושין works)

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a dispute of the תנאים?
phrases.notes: He means the earlier rule that a man cannot be מקדש a woman with a loan.

phrases.english: 'Be betrothed to me with a promissory note,'

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ מִלְוָה בְּיַד אֲחֵרִים
phrases.english: or he had a loan owed to him by others
and gave her the right to collect it from them,
Rabbi Meir says: she is betrothed,
and the Sages say: she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, now about the rule of קידושין with a loan rather than רב הונא's ax rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling, upheld in step 4, that one who is מקדש a woman with a loan does not make her מקודשת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי מאיר says a שטר חוב works for קידושין, the rule would follow only חכמים and would be a disputed position.

steps.title: The שטר חוב must be her own debt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons that the שטר חוב cannot be someone else's debt, because the ברייתא lists that as a separate case. So it must be her own debt to him, and the argument is about קידושין with a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of שטר חוב is this? If you say it is a note for others' debt, that is the same as 'a loan owed by others'! So isn't it a note for her own debt, and they argue about one who is מקדש with a loan?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds the proof. The ברייתא must be talking about a woman who owes him money, so the תנאים really are arguing about קידושין with a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mentions both 'a שטר חוב' and 'a loan owed by others.' If both meant other people's debts, the ברייתא would be saying the same thing twice. So the שטר חוב must record her own debt, and he is being מקדש her by cancelling it. That is exactly קידושין with a loan.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
If you say
That is the same as
Her own

phrases.english: This promissory note, what is the case?
If you say it is a promissory note of others,
that is the same as a loan owed by others!
Rather, is it not her own promissory note,
phrases.notes: She owes him money, and he lets the debt go as the קידושין.

phrases.english: and they argue about one who betroths with a loan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא quoted in step 11 proves the suggestion.
steps.raayaObject: That קידושין with a loan is a dispute between רבי מאיר and חכמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא lists 'a שטר חוב' separately from 'a loan owed by others', so the שטר חוב must be her own debt.

steps.title: Both cases are about others' debts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The שטר חוב really is someone else's debt. The two cases are different because one is a loan written in a שטר and the other is an oral loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is a note for others' debt. Here they argue about two cases: a loan written in a שטר, and a loan made by word of mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The ברייתא is not talking about her own debt at all, so it is not about קידושין with a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not repeat itself. 'שטר חוב' means another person's debt that is written in a document. 'מלוה ביד אחרים' means another person's debt that is only oral. So the rule against קידושין with a loan is not disputed by this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (keeping the original reading)
A loan recorded in a written document
An oral loan, with no document

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of debt here. 'Her own debt' would be קידושין with a loan. 'Others' debt' means he is giving her the right to collect a debt someone else owes him, which is a different case.

phrases.english: Actually, it is a promissory note of others,
and here, about a loan with a document
and about an oral loan, they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 12 by giving another way to read the ברייתא's two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case (written vs. oral debt of others)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שטר חוב must be her own debt, so the ברייתא is about קידושין with a loan.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases are debts owed by others. One is written and one is oral, so the rule about קידושין with a loan is not challenged.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof of step 12 that the ברייתא's שטר חוב is her own debt, so the ברייתא is not about קידושין with a loan
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases are not repetitive: 'שטר חוב' is others' written debt and 'מלוה ביד אחרים' is others' oral debt

steps.title: The written-debt case depends on רבי and חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the argument about a written debt. It follows the dispute between רבי and חכמים about whether a שטר is acquired just by handing it over, or only by writing a deed and handing it over.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a loan with a שטר, what do they argue about? They argue in the dispute of רבי and the חכמים. A ברייתא teaches: 'Letters' are acquired by handing over the document; these are the words of רבי. The חכמים say: whether he wrote but did not hand over, or handed over but did not write, the buyer has not acquired it until he both writes and hands over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why רבי מאיר and חכמים would argue about giving her someone else's written debt. It connects their argument to a well-known ברייתא about acquiring a שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, simply handing over the שטר transfers the debt, so the woman receives something of value and is מקודשת. That fits רבי מאיר. According to חכמים, he must also write a deed of transfer. Handing her the שטר alone gives her nothing, so she is not מקודשת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Letters': the debt written in a שטר
Handing over (the document)
A dispute
Wrote (a deed of transfer)

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute about how a שטר חוב is transferred to someone else comes up all over ש״ס in the laws of buying and selling debts.

phrases.english: With a loan with a document, about what do they disagree?
They disagree in the dispute of Rabbi and the Rabbis.
As it is taught: letters are acquired by handing over,
phrases.notes: 'Letters' means the debt written in the שטר, which can be passed to someone else.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בֵּין שֶׁכָּתַב וְלֹא מָסַר,
phrases.english: And the Sages say: whether he wrote but did not hand over,
phrases.notes: 'Wrote' means he wrote a separate deed saying he is transferring the debt.

phrases.english: or he handed over but did not write,
he has not acquired it until he writes and hands over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the reason for the written-debt half of the reading given in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about giving her a written debt owed by others?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They follow the dispute of רבי (handing over the שטר is enough) and חכמים (he must both write a deed and hand over).

steps.title: One side follows רבי and the other does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its first explanation: רבי מאיר holds like רבי, and חכמים do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds like רבי, and the other Sage does not hold like רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation it began in the last step. It tells us which side of the argument matches רבי and which side does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, a שטר is acquired just by handing it over, so רבי מאיר says the woman is מקודשת when she receives the שטר חוב. חכמים do not hold like רבי, so in their view she has not really received anything, and there is no קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'master.' Here it means 'one Sage' in an argument.
He holds that view, or agrees with it.
He does not hold that view, or does not agree with it.

phrases.english: One Sage holds like רבי
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר, who says she is מקודשת because the שטר passes to her just by handing it over.

phrases.english: and one Sage does not hold like רבי.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי וּמָר לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation from Step 14 by assigning each side of the argument to a view on רבי's rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר follows רבי (a שטר is acquired just by handing it over), so the קידושין works. חכמים reject רבי, so it does not.

steps.title: Second explanation: the argument is about רב פפא's rule
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: nobody holds like רבי. The argument is whether the seller of a שטר must write 'acquire it and all its liens,' as רב פפא says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say instead: nobody holds like רבי. Here they argue about רב פפא's rule. רב פפא said that someone who sells a שטר to his friend must write for him, 'Acquire it, it and all its liens.' One Sage holds like רב פפא, and one Sage does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different explanation of the same argument. Now both sides reject רבי, and the argument is about רב פפא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא says that when you sell a שטר, you must write 'acquire it and all its liens,' or else the debt itself does not pass. חכמים follow רב פפא, so without that writing the woman gets nothing. רבי מאיר does not follow רב פפא, so in his view the debt passes even without those words, and the קידושין works.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say...' This introduces another possible explanation.
Everyone. Here it means both sides of the argument.
They argue about this point.
Its liens: the legal rights to collect the debt, including from the borrower's property.
'Acquire for yourself.' This is the wording used to transfer ownership.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that selling a שטר may need more than handing over the paper. The rights to collect the debt also have to be transferred clearly.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
that everyone does not hold like רבי,
and here they argue about the rule of רב פפא,
as רב פפא said:
someone who sells a שטר to his friend
must write for him:
"Acquire for yourself it and all its liens."
One Sage holds like רב פפא,
phrases.notes: This is חכמים. Without that writing, the woman gets nothing.

phrases.english: and one Sage does not hold like רב פפא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לֵית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation in Steps 14-15 with a different reason for the argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both sides reject רבי. חכמים require רב פפא's wording for the debt to pass. רבי מאיר does not, so in his view the קידושין works without it.

steps.title: Third explanation begins: the argument is about שמואל's rule
steps.stepSummary: A third explanation: everyone accepts רב פפא's rule. The argument is about a ruling of שמואל, which the text is about to quote.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say instead: everyone holds like רב פפא, and here they argue about the rule of שמואל, as שמואל said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a third explanation and is setting up the next move. It names שמואל's rule but does not quote it yet; the quote comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now even רבי מאיר agrees that the 'acquire it and all its liens' wording is needed. So the argument cannot be about רב פפא. It must depend on something else, a rule of שמואל, which will explain why חכמים still think the קידושין might not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, meaning in this argument between רבי מאיר and חכמים.
'As he said.' This introduces a quote.

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל's actual words come in the next part of the text. Do not try to guess his rule from this line alone.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
phrases.english: that everyone holds like רב פפא
and here they argue about the rule of שמואל.
As שמואל said:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside the רב פפא explanation from Step 16 by saying both sides accept it. It moves the argument to a rule of שמואל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both sides accept רב פפא. The argument depends on שמואל's rule, which the next part of the text will quote.
